patterns.name: 句首「Of course」
patterns.context: 引号内以 Of course 引出让步或补充说明，谈便利设施。
patterns.domain: 关于家务与技术的评论文字

patterns.name: 连续限定词与数字
patterns.trigger: 「In»4« every»6« period»4« t»4« a»8« generation」及「4»5« Each»6« member」
patterns.context: 经济学论述中出现 period、generation 等词，以及紧邻的数字和 Each。

patterns.name: 基础性问题句
patterns.context: 谈政治信念时，以 how do we 引出解释性问题。

patterns.name: 其他分散激活
patterns.context: 分别出现在不自然的网页片段、银行贷款相关文本及家务便利话题中；未见稳定共享的词义或句法条件。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、金融相关文本、家庭生活评论

en.description: Activation is dispersed across segments, focusing on common words, title words, and internal subwords, including nearly, an, the, We, Each, and EVERY. Although several text types can be identified, no stable semantic or grammatical condition is apparent.

patterns.name: Random internal subwords and tokenization boundaries
patterns.context: Trigger positions are scattered, often within common words, at sentence beginnings, or on internal subwords; there is no stable local semantic condition across segments
patterns.domain: Cross-corpus and cross-genre; may involve word fragments or common words, but evidence is insufficient to establish a specific pattern

patterns.name: Biomedical abstract fragment
patterns.context: Appears in the opening phrase «Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope.»

patterns.name: EVERY in a title or proper name
patterns.context: Appears in the all-caps title/lyrics «THE PATH OF EVERYONE», the album name «Every Band Has...», or educational copy «Each student...»; capitalization and following words vary
patterns.domain: Music catalogs, educational promotion, title text

patterns.name: Sentence-initial We
patterns.context: Appears in the title «How We Do It», followed by a line break and another passage

patterns.name: Group in a category or organization name
patterns.context: Immediately follows a Q&A marker and line break, followed by «/organize program icons and files»

patterns.name: Common words in financial advertising
patterns.context: Appears in loan promotional copy, but these words also occur in other segments, so finance-specific semantic activation cannot be established

patterns.name: Scattered words in a neurotechnology project description
patterns.context: Appears at the end of a description of a nervous-system therapy project for veterans; there is no stable evidence of specialized terminology triggering activation

patterns.name: Scattered words in catalogs/abstracts
patterns.context: Appears in biology abstracts, journal information, and keyword fragments; the relationship between trigger words and topic is unclear

9_2056.description: 激活散布于各段，集中在常见词、标题词及词内子词，包含 nearly、an、the、We、Each、EVERY 等；虽可列出若干文体片段，但看不出稳定语义或语法条件。

patterns.name: 随机内部子词与分词边界
patterns.trigger: 如 «nearly»、«in»、«an»、«the»、«should»、«Each»、«We»、«every»、«Focus»、«Group»；多处激活落在词的一部分，如 «EX»、«ML»、«Shared»?（原文 « shared»）、«cal»、«velop»、«trans»、«Experience» 中的 «ience»
patterns.context: 触发位置分散，常位于常见词、句首或词内子词；各段间没有稳定一致的局部语义条件
patterns.domain: 跨语料、跨文体；可能涉及词片段或常见词，但证据不足以确立具体模式

patterns.name: 生物医学摘要片段
patterns.context: 出现在摘要开头短语 «Experience with an ultrasound stethoscope.» 中

patterns.name: 标题或专名中的 EVERY
patterns.context: 出现在大写标题/歌词 «THE PATH OF EVERYONE»、专辑名 «Every Band Has...»，或教育文案 «Each student...»；大小写和后续词各异
patterns.domain: 音乐目录、教育宣传、标题文本

patterns.name: 句首 We
patterns.context: 出现在标题 «How We Do It» 中，之后接换行和另一段文字

patterns.name: 栏目或组织名中的 Group
patterns.context: 紧接问答标记与换行，后接 «/organize program icons and files»

patterns.name: 金融广告常见词
patterns.context: 出现在借贷宣传文案，但这些词也在其他段出现，无法证明是金融语义特异反应

patterns.name: 神经科技项目描述中的零散词
patterns.context: 出现在面向退伍军人的神经系统疗法项目描述末尾；没有稳定的专业术语触发证据

patterns.name: 目录/摘要中的零散词
patterns.context: 出现在生物学摘要、期刊信息和关键词碎片中，触发词与主题的对应关系不明确
patterns.domain: 生物医学及文献目录文本

en.description: Activation is distributed across internal fragments of multiple words and short words in various domains; it often occurs alongside capitalized titles, catalog formatting, or broken concatenated text. Trigger positions vary across segments, and no reliable single semantic or syntactic condition has been identified.

patterns.name: Initial fragments after tokenization
patterns.context: Activation often falls on internal English word fragments or subword fragments at the beginnings of adjacent words, especially short tokens such as «Each», «an», and «/»; it is not tied to a fixed complete word or semantic meaning.

patterns.name: Capitalized words at sentence openings or in titles
patterns.context: Strong activation appears near capitalized words, title words, or sentence-initial words, but the specific words and contexts vary considerably.
patterns.domain: Web, medical abstracts, Q&A, patents, and catalog text

patterns.name: Common short words in broken or corrupted text
patterns.context: Passages contain clear concatenation, disorder, or incoherence; activation focuses on high-frequency short words or local word fragments, with no stable topical condition apparent.

patterns.name: Catalog and numbering formats
patterns.context: Activation appears near tables of contents, chapter numbering, Roman numerals, and title formatting; it falls on different fragments, so it is unclear whether the format itself is the trigger.
patterns.domain: Book tables of contents and technical documents

patterns.name: Financial-word adjacency
patterns.context: A group of activations occurs near financial words such as loans, interest rates, and repayments, but the text is heavily fragmented, making it impossible to determine whether the trigger is financial semantics.

patterns.name: Clearly unrelated anomalous concatenations
patterns.context: Multiple unrelated fragments activate in text with semantic jumps, concatenated words, or apparent machine-generated/crawl noise.

9_2056.description: 激活分布在多领域、多个词内部片段及短词上；常伴标题大写、目录格式或破碎拼接文本。各段触发位置不一致，暂无可靠的单一语义或句法条件。

patterns.name: 分词后的词首片段
patterns.context: 激活常落在英语词的内部或相邻词首的子词片段上，尤其是「Each」「an」「/」等短 token；并非固定完整词或固定语义。

patterns.name: 句首或标题式大写词
patterns.context: 大写词、标题词或句首词附近出现较强激活，但具体词和语境差别很大。
patterns.domain: 网页、医学摘要、问答、专利及目录文本

patterns.name: 被破碎或乱码文本中的常见短词
patterns.context: 段落含有明显拼接、错乱或不连贯文本；激活集中在高频短词或局部词片段，未见稳定主题条件。

patterns.name: 目录与编号格式
patterns.trigger: «VOL»2. II.；«CONT»3ENTS« OF»1« V»3«OL»2. II.；«I»2«.»2；«1»6« Table»6« of»5« Contents»4
patterns.context: 目录、章节编号、罗马数字及标题排版附近出现激活；强度落在不同片段，不能确认是格式本身触发。

patterns.name: 金融词汇邻接
patterns.context: 贷款、利率、还款等金融词汇附近有一组激活，但文本严重破碎，无法确定触发条件是否为金融语义。

patterns.name: 明显无关的异常拼接
patterns.trigger: «rel»5«inger»2« Archives»5 download The National Basketball« still»7；«episode»7« audi»4«ob»3«ook»5
patterns.context: 语义跳跃、词语拼接或类似机器生成/抓取噪声的文本中，多个不相干片段激活。

en.description: Activation is primarily associated with an and several internal word fragments, especially in segmented proper nouns, words, and research text; scattered triggers also include all, years, drug names, and chemical names, without forming a stable semantic pattern.

patterns.name: Word-internal suffix “ing”
patterns.context: High activation falls on a later subword fragment within a segmented word or adjective; one example is not ing, possibly indicating a broader pattern of internal word fragments.

patterns.name: Tokenization of the indefinite article an
patterns.context: Activation concentrates on the indefinite article an, followed by different words such as ultrasound, exceptionally, operational, and objective.
patterns.domain: Medical abstracts, research text, and email

patterns.name: Internal subwords in proper nouns or words
patterns.context: Words are split into multiple tokens, with activation biased toward internal fragments; examples include experience, eSpeak, and Quatro, but their meanings differ.

patterns.name: Suffix or internal fragment “eth/et”
patterns.context: Internal word segmentation occurs, but not all similar fragments activate strongly; it is unclear whether a specific suffix is the trigger.

patterns.name: all in a quotation
patterns.context: Appears at the beginning of a quoted sentence, followed by “of the various demonstrations”; this is a single example, with no confirmable condition.

patterns.name: Initial repetition of the proper noun Quatro
patterns.context: The same word appears repeatedly at the beginning of an entry, with the segmented parts Qu/atro activating; this may relate to internal word fragments such as eSpeak in other materials.

patterns.name: Various scattered subword activations
patterns.context: Ordinary words and years in historical text, internal fragments of drug names, and initial fragments of chemical structure names activate separately, with no shared semantics or stable contextual condition apparent.
patterns.domain: Historical art history, medicine, chemical abstracts

patterns.name: Structural markers and section-initial elements
patterns.context: Medical paper subsection headings, separator lines, and elements at the beginning of following sections; headings and markers themselves activate weakly, with strong activation mainly on an.

9_2056.description: 激活以 an 及若干词内子词片段为主，尤其出现在拆分的专名、词语和科研文本中；另有 all、年份、药物与化学名称等零散触发，未形成稳定语义模式。

patterns.name: 词内后缀“ing”
patterns.context: 高激活落在分词或形容词内部的后续子词片段；一个例子并非 ing，可能只是更广泛的词内片段模式。
patterns.domain: 科研摘要及研究资助文本

patterns.name: 不定冠词 an 的分词
patterns.context: 激活集中在不定冠词 an；其后接 ultrasound、exceptionally、operational、objective 等不同词。
patterns.domain: 医学摘要、科研文本及邮件

patterns.name: 专名或词语的内部子词
patterns.context: 词语被拆成多个 token，激活偏向内部片段；包含 experience、eSpeak 和 Quatro，但具体词义各异。

patterns.name: 后缀或词内片段“eth/et”
patterns.context: 出现词内拆分，但并非所有同类片段都强激活；是否由特定后缀触发不明确。
patterns.domain: 医学文本、历史艺术文本

patterns.name: 引语中的 all
patterns.context: 位于引号中的句子开头，后接“of the various demonstrations”；仅此一例，缺少可确认条件。

patterns.name: 专名 Quatro 的词首复现
patterns.context: 同一词在条目开头重复出现，拆分部分 Qu/atro 激活；与其他材料中的 eSpeak 等词内片段可能相关。

patterns.name: 多种零散子词激活
patterns.context: 历史文本中的普通词和年份、药物名称的词内片段、化学结构名称的词首片段分别激活，未见共同语义或稳定上下文条件。
patterns.domain: 历史艺术史、医学、化学摘要

patterns.name: 结构标记与段首成分
patterns.context: 医学论文小节标题、分隔线及其后段首成分；标题和标记本身激活较弱，强激活主要出现在 an。

en.description: Strong activations are distributed across the subwords in washout and hyperpolarization, repeated name fragments in EuroParl, numeric table formats, and several ordinary English words or pronouns. Aside from triggers within some subwords, no consistent semantic or contextual pattern is evident.

patterns.name: wash in “washout”
patterns.context: Appears in the biological abstract term “washout resistance”; activation is concentrated in the beginning of washout.

patterns.name: polar in a hyperpolarization term
patterns.context: Appears in a technical term describing activity-dependent chronic hyperpolarization.

patterns.name: Subwords in names
patterns.context: These subwords appear in consecutive repeated name fragments; the same string is repeated in two paragraphs, and another similar string also triggers activation.
patterns.domain: Names or proper nouns in EuroParl text

patterns.name: Format markers in numeric tables
patterns.context: Several decimal-like values recur in a sequence of numbered data; activation is scattered, with no clear trigger tied to a single number.

patterns.name: Sporadic triggers in general English text
patterns.context: Appear respectively in “never goes offline,” a narrative context with the pronoun he, and the subword fragment “androgynous”; no identifiable shared contextual condition links them.

9_2194.description: 强激活分散于 washout、hyperpolarization 的词片、EuroParl 中重复姓名片段、数值表格格式，以及若干普通英语词语或代词；除部分词片内部触发外，未见统一语义或上下文模式。

patterns.name: “washout”中的 wash
patterns.context: 出现在生物学摘要的术语 “washout resistance” 中；激活集中于 washout 的开头部分。

patterns.name: 超极化术语中的 polar
patterns.context: 出现在描述神经活动依赖性慢性超极化的专业术语中。

patterns.name: 人名中的词片
patterns.context: 这些词片出现在连续重复的人名/姓名片段中；同一串在两个段落重复，另一个相似串也触发。
patterns.domain: EuroParl 文本中的姓名或专名

patterns.name: 数字表格中的格式符
patterns.context: 一行按序号列出的数值数据中，多个类似小数的数值反复出现；激活较分散，未见明显单一数字触发。

patterns.name: 一般英语文本中的零散触发
patterns.context: 分别出现在 “never goes offline”、代词 he 的叙述语境，以及单词片段 “androgynous” 中；彼此缺少可确认的共同上下文条件。

en.description: Activations are distributed across hyperpolarization terminology, washout, fragments within long words or proper nouns, expressions of an ongoing state with never, and email salutation/signature formats; trigger points and contexts vary considerably.

patterns.name: hyperpolarization terminology
patterns.context: In neuroscience or physiology titles describing hyperpolarization and related factors; activation falls on multiple subword fragments within the term.

patterns.name: washout in a technical term
patterns.context: In a biology paper title, washout appears with resistance to describe resistance to the washout of an effect.

patterns.name: Fragments within proper nouns or word forms
patterns.context: Activation is distributed across subword fragments within longer words or proper nouns; examples involve a title word, a place name, a tumor type, and a vascular malformation, with no shared semantic condition.
patterns.domain: Web text, encyclopedias, and PubMed abstracts

patterns.name: never and ongoing states
patterns.context: The sentence says an entity has continually maintained a state or activity: a music service “never goes offline,” or a church “never ceased operating.”

patterns.name: Email line breaks and salutations
patterns.context: Email salutations and line breaks, or names, titles, and line breaks in signatures; activation falls mainly on formatting markers and name/title fragments.

9_2194.description: 激活分散于超极化术语、washout、长词或专名内部片段、never 持续状态表达，以及邮件称呼/签名格式；各例触发点与语境差异较大。

patterns.name: hyperpolarization terminology
patterns.context: 神经科学或生理学标题中，描述超极化及相关因子；激活落在术语内部多个子词片段上。
patterns.domain: PubMed 摘要，神经科学/生理学

patterns.name: 专业词中的 washout
patterns.context: 生物学论文标题中，washout 与 resistance 连用，描述某种效应的洗脱抵抗性。

patterns.name: 专名或词形内部的片段
patterns.context: 激活分布在较长词或专名内部的子词片段；这些例子分别涉及标题中的词、地名、肿瘤类型和血管畸形，未见共同语义条件。
patterns.domain: 网页文本、百科和 PubMed 摘要

patterns.name: never 与持续状态
patterns.context: 句中说明某对象一直未停止某种状态或活动：歌曲服务“never goes offline”，教堂“never ceased operating”。

patterns.name: 邮件换行与称呼
patterns.context: 邮件正文的称呼和换行，或签名中的姓名、职务及换行；激活主要落在格式标记和姓名/职位片段。

en.description: Activations cover varied formats: music encyclopedia entries, transitions between definitions and theorems in mathematics papers, project and medical abstracts, garbled legal text, payment error-handling code, and email headers. The patterns differ considerably, with no reliable shared meaning or semantic trigger.

patterns.name: Release descriptions in song/album entries
patterns.context: A music entry begins with a title or work name, followed by information about the singer/band, work type, and release; activation often falls on common narrative words and “label.”

patterns.name: Transitions between definitions and theorems in mathematics papers
patterns.context: Transition language in a mathematics paper, after formal objects, sets, or thresholds, leading into a definition or a review of a theorem.

patterns.name: Project proposals and descriptions of research subjects
patterns.context: A project proposal lists research topics and describes experimental factors or research subjects.

patterns.name: Medical title-like phrases
patterns.context: A paper-title fragment consisting of a disease/tumor category followed by a colon and a research description.

patterns.name: Unusual characters or garbled text
patterns.context: The text consists mainly of illegible symbols and letter fragments, with no stable, readable semantic structure.

patterns.name: Error handling and error-code checks
patterns.context: Catches a payment connection exception, reads the exception data, and checks whether it contains a specified error code.

patterns.name: Raw email message headers
patterns.context: Email header fields in forwarded or quoted content, followed by the sender and send time.

9_2194.description: 激活覆盖多种格式：音乐百科作品介绍、数学论文的定义/定理衔接、项目与医学摘要、乱码法律文本、支付异常代码及邮件头。可见模式彼此差异较大，尚无可靠共同词义或语义触发点。

patterns.name: 歌曲/专辑条目中的发行描述
patterns.trigger: “is a debut single by”“song … was released as a single”“studio album … was released on”“sub-label”
patterns.context: 音乐作品条目以标题或作品名开头，随后介绍歌手/乐队、作品类型及发行信息；激活常落在常见叙述词及“label”等词上。

patterns.name: 数学论文中的定义与定理衔接
patterns.context: 数学论文在形式化对象、集合或阈值后，转入定义或回顾定理的段落衔接语。

patterns.name: 项目提案与研究对象描述
patterns.trigger: “Proposed projects include:”以及“effect of ions … potassium and calcium”
patterns.context: 项目提案列举研究内容，并说明实验因素或研究对象。

patterns.name: 医学题名式短语
patterns.context: 以疾病/肿瘤类别加冒号及研究说明构成的论文题名片段。

patterns.name: 异常字符或乱码文本
patterns.context: 文本主要由难以辨认的符号、字母片段组成，缺少可读的稳定语义结构。

patterns.name: 异常处理与错误码检查
patterns.context: 捕获支付连接异常，读取异常数据并检查其中是否含指定错误码。

patterns.name: 邮件原始消息头
patterns.context: 邮件转发或引用内容中的邮件头字段，后接发件人及发送时间。

en.description: The strongest activation usually falls on few in a few. Other sporadic triggers include the relative pronoun who, Then at the start of mathematical derivations or narrative sentences, the proper-name fragment Bel, and the stock abbreviation TX; these span domains with no single stable meaning.

patterns.name: few / a few phrases
patterns.context: The quantifier a few modifies a count noun; the strongest activation falls on few
patterns.domain: Spoken language, forum discussions, and general narrative

patterns.name: who in relative clauses
patterns.context: who introduces a relative clause modifying person
patterns.domain: Patent background sections, formal explanatory prose

patterns.name: Then introducing a derivation step
patterns.context: In a mathematical derivation, introduces subsequent conditions and definitions after a formula or assumption

patterns.name: Bel fragment in the proper noun Belgrave
patterns.context: A word begins with Bel; the same passage also contains proper-name fragments such as Belgrave and Beltrami

patterns.name: Then in theological quotations
patterns.context: In a biblical parable quotation, Then appears at the beginning of a narrative sentence

patterns.name: TX company abbreviation fragment
patterns.context: TX appears within a company abbreviation in a stock example

patterns.name: Other unexplained sporadic activations
patterns.context: Local word fragments or tokenization boundaries vary; the available context is insufficient to identify a stable condition

9_2194.description: 最强处多落在 a few 的 few；另有关系代词 who、数学推导或叙事句首的 Then、Bel 专名片段及股票缩写 TX 等零散触发，跨领域且无单一稳定语义。

patterns.name: few／a few 的短语
patterns.trigger: “a few pulls”“a few months”“a few years”“a few programming languages”中的 «few»9/10
patterns.context: 出现量词 a few，修饰可数名词；激活最强处落在 few
patterns.domain: 口语、论坛讨论及一般叙述

patterns.name: 关系从句中的 who
patterns.context: who 引导修饰 person 的关系从句
patterns.domain: 专利背景技术、正式说明文

patterns.name: Then 引出推导步骤
patterns.context: 数学推导中，在公式或假设之后引出后续条件与定义

patterns.name: Belgrave 专名片段
patterns.context: 单词以 Bel 开头；同段还出现 Belgrave、Beltrami 等专名片段
patterns.domain: 百科条目、专利医学文本

patterns.name: 神学引文中的 Then
patterns.context: 圣经寓言引文中，Then 位于叙事句首
patterns.domain: 维基百科宗教条目、圣经引文

patterns.name: TX 公司缩写片段
patterns.context: 股票举例中，公司名缩写内部出现 TX

patterns.name: unexplained 其余零散激活
patterns.trigger: 未发现可由上述模式解释的明确共同触发项；如 “«happ»”“«cra»”“«re»generative”
patterns.context: 局部词片段或分词边界各异，现有上下文不足以确定稳定条件

en.concept: English syntactic introducers and title words
en.description: Activations often fall on linking or introducing elements such as that, when, what, and Will; a medical proper-name fragment, Spindle, also appears once. A few passages have title or explanatory prose structures, while the passage about an Irish band has no clear corresponding clue.

patterns.name: that as a sentence connector
patterns.context: that is followed by a clause, temporal/relative clause, or statement; it recurs within the passage

patterns.name: Will in an interrogative title
patterns.context: In a title-like question, Will appears after the subject or noun phrase and expresses the future or a need

patterns.name: that in relative clauses
patterns.context: that introduces a relative clause describing a noun, as in “centers that offers” and “issues that can prevent”

patterns.name: what as a condition or topic introducer
patterns.context: what at the beginning of a sentence or clause introduces the matter being asked about or discussed

patterns.name: when in temporal/conditional clauses
patterns.context: Introduces a temporal or situational clause, followed by a description of what happens in that circumstance

patterns.name: Repeated fragment of a technical name
patterns.context: A tumor name recurs in a medical title; strong activation falls on its segmented subword fragments

patterns.name: that as a determiner
patterns.context: that occurs in demonstrative constructions referring to previously mentioned content, as in “that period” or “that …”

9_2194.concept: 英语句法引导词与标题词
9_2194.description: 激活多落在 that、when、what、Will 等连接或引导成分上，也出现一次医学专名片段 Spindle；少数段落呈标题或说明文结构，爱尔兰乐队段无明显对应线索。

patterns.name: 句中连接词 that
patterns.context: that 后接从句、时间/关系从句或陈述内容；在段落中反复出现

patterns.name: 疑问标题中的 Will
patterns.context: 标题式疑问句中，Will 位于主语或名词短语之后，表示未来/需求

patterns.name: 关系从句 that
patterns.context: that 引导描述名词的关系从句，如“centers that offers”“issues that can prevent”
patterns.domain: 百科说明、产品/实用说明

patterns.name: 条件或话题引入词 what
patterns.context: 句首或从句开头的 what 引出所询问、讨论的内容

patterns.name: 时间/条件从句 when
patterns.context: 引出时间或情境从句，后续说明某时发生的状况

patterns.name: 重复的专业名称片段
patterns.context: 医学标题中重复出现的肿瘤名称；高激活落在被拆分词片段上

patterns.name: 限定词 that
patterns.context: that 位于指示性结构中，指向此前提到的内容，如“that period”“that …”

en.description: All ten passages show strong activation (usually 9 or 10) on the relative word «which», in both relative clauses and supplementary clauses. In a few contexts, pronouns or predicates within the clause also activate more weakly.

patterns.name: which in relative clauses
patterns.context: Appears at the start of a relative or supplementary clause within a sentence, followed by an auxiliary, pronoun, or predicate; activation is not limited to a particular meaning or grammatical domain.

patterns.name: Full relative-clause structure
patterns.context: Relative clauses often add information after a preceding noun or proposition; as in the previous pattern, but activation may also be sensitive to the subsequent relative-clause structure.
patterns.domain: Books, academic writing, encyclopedias, forums, emails, and legal text

patterns.name: Subjects or referring expressions within which-clauses
patterns.context: Referring words or predicates within relative clauses sometimes also receive positive activation; for example, «which they are able to give» and «which were included».

9_2194.description: 十段均在关系词«which»处出现强激活（多为9或10），涵盖关系从句与补充说明用法；少数上下文中从句内的代词或谓语也有较弱激活。

patterns.name: 关系从句中的 which
patterns.context: 出现于句中关系从句或补充说明从句的引导位置，后接助动词、代词或谓语；激活不局限于特定意义或语法领域。

patterns.name: 完整关系从句结构
patterns.trigger: «which»后接从句内容，如«which will show»、«which can be found»、«which is really beautiful»
patterns.context: 相对从句常在前文名词或命题之后补充说明；与前一模式相同，但可能还对后续关系从句结构敏感。
patterns.domain: 书籍、学术、百科、论坛、邮件及法律文本

patterns.name: which从句中的主语或指代形式
patterns.context: 关系从句中的指代词或谓语有时也获正激活；例如«which they are able to give»、«which were included»。

en.description: The most stable trigger is who in relative clauses; if, When, and interrogative or subordinate introducers such as where/how also activate strongly. Several scattered pronouns, sentence-initial It, and ordinary it also activate, but cannot be explained by a single pattern.

patterns.name: Relative pronoun who introducing information about people
patterns.context: who follows a noun referring to a person or group and introduces a relative clause describing their identity, experience, attributes, or actions; activation is concentrated on who itself.
patterns.domain: Multiple genres: biographies, historical argument, religious texts, encyclopedia entries, and general dialogue

patterns.name: if introducing a condition or hypothesis
patterns.context: if introduces a conditional or hypothetical clause; examples concern whether there is truth and a hypothetical dishonest answer to avoid embarrassment.

patterns.name: When as a temporal introducer
patterns.context: When introduces a historical situation or temporal clause, followed by a description of an event or circumstance.

patterns.name: where as an interrogative word
patterns.context: In a series of fundamental questions about life or the world, where asks about origin.

patterns.name: how as an interrogative word
patterns.context: At the beginning of a question giving an example or asking about the cause of an event, asks how it happened.

patterns.name: What as an interrogative word
patterns.context: In dialogue, What introduces a hypothetical follow-up question; activation is weaker here.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial It in information structure
patterns.context: Sentence-initial It picks up the previous context and begins a statement about a preceding result or situation, rather than a salient question or relative clause.

patterns.name: Lexical or tokenized it
patterns.context: Used as a pronoun or dummy subject in ordinary sentences, appearing in a judgment about chance and a description of a natural process; unlike the high-activation interrogative-word pattern.

patterns.name: Other context-dependent pronoun triggers
patterns.context: Pronouns occur in different syntactic positions: he as the subject of a report, ones referring to care programs, you as the addressee of a question, and we in a parallel question about identity/origin; they do not form a unified syntactic pattern.
patterns.domain: News, online dialogue, religious texts, and encyclopedia text

9_2194.description: 最稳定的触发是关系从句中的 who，另对 if、When 及 where/how 等疑问或从属引导词有较强激活；另有若干分散的代词、句首 It 与普通 it 激活，不能统一解释。

patterns.name: 关系代词 who 引出人物说明
patterns.context: who 位于人物或群体名词之后，引出其身份、经历、属性或行动的关系从句；激活集中在 who 本身。
patterns.domain: 多种文体：人物传记、历史议论、宗教文本、百科条目及一般对话

patterns.name: 条件或假设引导词 if
patterns.context: if 引出条件或假设从句；分别涉及是否有真相，以及为避免尴尬而作不诚实回答的假设。

patterns.name: 时间引导词 When
patterns.context: When 引出历史情境或时间从句，后接事件或情境描述。
patterns.domain: 引述、历史或公共议题论述

patterns.name: 疑问词 where
patterns.context: 在提出人生或世界根本问题的并列疑问中，用 where 询问来源。

patterns.name: 疑问词 how
patterns.context: 在举例或追问事件缘由的疑问句开头，询问事情如何发生。

patterns.name: 疑问词 What
patterns.context: 在对话中以 What 引出假设性追问；该处激活较弱。

patterns.name: 信息结构中的句首 It
patterns.context: 句首 It 承接前文，开启对前述结果或情况的陈述，而非显著的疑问或关系从句。

patterns.name: 特定词汇／分词 it
patterns.context: 在普通句中作代词或形式主语，分别出现在 chance 判断及自然过程的叙述中；与高激活的疑问词模式不同。

patterns.name: 语境性强的其他代词触发
patterns.context: 代词处于不同句法位置：he 作报道中的主语，ones 指代照护项目，you 作提问对象，we 出现在身份／来源的并列问题中；无法归为统一句法模式。
patterns.domain: 新闻、网络对话、宗教及百科文本

en.concept: Generic reference and expressions of possibility, with additional domain-word triggers
en.description: Activations are scattered: common patterns include generic entities or scope (anyone, anything, any), possibility and inferential questions. Other local patterns include quantum algorithms, reviews of books for boys, fragmented Spanish subwords, and negation.

patterns.name: Generic entities and ranges
patterns.context: In statements about privacy, cost, ability, behavior, or possibility, words referring generically to people, things, or scope activate, often in expressions like anything/anyone.

patterns.name: Questions and possibility inferences
patterns.context: When raising or discussing possibilities, inferences, or imaginings, activations appear near interrogative words, modal verbs, or generic objects.

patterns.name: Quantum algorithm topic words
patterns.context: When introducing research progress, papers, or reviews on quantum algorithms, activation is strongest on algorithms at the end of the topic phrase.

patterns.name: Spanish tokenization and negation
patterns.context: In continuous Spanish text, multiple words are split into subword tokens; the negation word no has the strongest activation in the sentence.

patterns.name: Suitability of a book for boys
patterns.context: Evaluates whether a book is suitable for boys to read; nearby text discusses literary quality, interest, or publication.

patterns.name: Word-initial fragments and proper nouns
patterns.context: Activation is distributed across fragmented Spanish subwords and several common short fragments in sentences, with no stable semantic condition corresponding to the other passages.

9_2194.concept: 泛指与可能性表达，兼有领域词触发
9_2194.description: 激活较分散：常见于泛指对象或范围（anyone、anything、any）、可能性与疑问推断；另有量子算法、男孩读物评价、西班牙语碎片化子词及否定词等局部模式。

patterns.name: 泛指对象与数量范围
patterns.context: 在关于隐私、费用、能力、行为或可能性的陈述中，泛指人、事物或范围的词受到激活，常出现在 anything/anyone 一类表达里。

patterns.name: 疑问结构与可能性推断
patterns.context: 提出或讨论可能性、推断、想象时，疑问词、情态动词或泛指宾语附近出现激活。

patterns.name: 量子算法主题词
patterns.context: 介绍量子算法研究进展、论文或综述时，主题短语末尾的 algorithms 激活最强。

patterns.name: 西班牙语分词与否定词
patterns.context: 西班牙语连续文本中，多个词被切分成子词标记；句中否定词 no 激活最强。

patterns.name: 书籍对男孩的适读评价
patterns.context: 评价书籍适合男孩阅读，周围谈及文学质量、趣味或出版情况。

patterns.name: 词首残片与专名
patterns.context: 激活分布在西班牙语词语的碎片化子词以及句中若干常见短片段，未见与其他段落稳定对应的语义条件。

en.description: Primarily responds to structures asking about recommendations, processes, or conditions, especially combinations of what/how/does/should. It also responds more weakly or sporadically to hypothetical questions and generic references to events.

patterns.name: should + person + verb in questions
patterns.context: In a question introduced by an interrogative word, should is followed by a subject and verb to ask about advice, steps, timing, or what should be done; activation often concentrates on should and the adjacent interrogative structure

patterns.name: does / do question structures
patterns.context: does (and related do constructions) follows an interrogative word or subject, introducing a question about mechanisms, outcomes, or conditions

patterns.name: broken/must be degree constructions in questions
patterns.context: how introduces a question, while must and be form a judgment about degree or necessity; activation concentrates on words such as broken and must

patterns.name: Asking what valuable things would still be produced
patterns.context: what kind of is followed by a noun, and would still forms a hypothetical question; activation is concentrated on valuable things would still

patterns.name: Generic event expressions with something like that
patterns.context: Refers generically to something that may happen in the future, with something and like that used together; the passage also includes a prior prediction about “something like that happening”

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问句中询问建议、过程或条件的结构，尤其是 what/how/does/should 等词的组合；另对假设性提问及泛指事件表达有较弱或零星响应。

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 should + 人称 + 动词
patterns.trigger: “What should I…”, “What should you…”, “How long should I…”；尤其是 should
patterns.context: 疑问词引导的问题中，should 后接主语和动词，用于询问建议、步骤、时间或应做之事；激活常集中在 should 及紧邻的疑问结构

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 does / do 提问结构
patterns.context: 疑问词或主语后出现 does（以及相关的 do 类结构），引出对机制、结果或条件的询问

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 broken/must be 程度结构
patterns.context: how 引导疑问，must 与 be 构成程度或必要性判断；激活集中在 broken、must 等词

patterns.name: 询问仍会产出的有价值事物
patterns.trigger: “what kind of valuable things would still be produced?”
patterns.context: what kind of 后接名词，would still be 构成假设性提问；激活集中在 valuable things would still

patterns.name: something like that 的泛指事件表达
patterns.context: 对未来可能发生的某事作泛指，something 与 like that 连用；该段还包含前文对“something like that happening”的预测

en.description: Most passages activate on something generic and not yet specifically named, especially when followed by a description or a that-clause; common in forum discussions evaluating ideas, uses, and feasibility. There are also examples of things referring to opinions or topics, and an isolated pattern involving studies in a medical abstract.

patterns.name: Indefinite entity in something that constructions
patterns.context: Discusses an object, project, thing, or phenomenon that has not yet been specifically named; usually something in a main clause, also including a modifying clause introduced by something that
patterns.domain: Spoken dialogue and Hacker News forum discussions

patterns.name: Feasibility or usefulness evaluation
patterns.context: Evaluates whether an idea, website, technology, or thing is useful, popular, or commercially viable; often includes evaluative words such as useful, popular, market, and money
patterns.domain: Hacker News startup, software, and technology discussions

patterns.name: Entities in conditional or degree clauses
patterns.context: something is the subject of a clause discussing the extent to which something holds, conditions it meets, or outcomes it causes
patterns.domain: Repair Q&A; etymology and definition discussions

patterns.name: Future or hypothetical events
patterns.context: something refers to a possible event or goal that has not yet occurred or been achieved; it is governed by constructions such as seeing, happening, or enough to

patterns.name: Things someone is doing or discussing
patterns.context: things/something refers to someone's opinions or topics of personal interest, rather than a product or concrete object
patterns.domain: Comments and discussions about personal websites

patterns.name: Non-primary pattern: studies in medical papers
patterns.context: In a formal academic sentence, studies refers to subsequent research; activation is concentrated on studies and neighboring words, without the previously described something construction

9_2194.description: 多数片段激活于泛指、尚未具体命名的 something，尤其是其后带描述或 that 从句时；常见于论坛中评价构想、用途与可行性。另有 things 指观点或话题的用例，以及医学摘要中 studies 的孤立模式。

patterns.name: something that 式不定对象
patterns.trigger: “something”后接“like that”“that will look good”“very similar”“useful”等描述，或形成“something that …”结构
patterns.context: 在谈论一个尚未具体命名的对象、项目、事物或现象；多为主句中的 something，亦包括 something that 引出的修饰从句
patterns.domain: 口语对话及 HackerNews 论坛讨论

patterns.name: 可行性或用途评估
patterns.trigger: “something useful”“something popular enough”“something … becoming a big money”“something useful that has a market price”
patterns.context: 评估构想、网站、技术或事物是否有用、受欢迎、能否商业化；常出现 useful、popular、market、money 等评价词
patterns.domain: HackerNews 创业、软件、科技讨论

patterns.name: 条件或程度从句中的事物
patterns.trigger: “how broken must something be”以及“something that is so disgusting that…”
patterns.context: something 是从句主语；讨论达到何种程度、满足何种条件，或某事物造成的结果
patterns.domain: 维修问答；词源、释义讨论

patterns.name: 将来或假设中发生的事
patterns.trigger: “seeing something like that happening”“something popular enough to reach…”
patterns.context: something 指尚未发生或尚未实现的可能事件、目标；受 seeing、happening 或 enough to 等结构支配
patterns.domain: 口语推测；互联网产品讨论

patterns.name: 某人正在做或谈论的事
patterns.trigger: “seeing things this way”“writing … about something they are passionate about”
patterns.context: things/something 指人的看法或个人感兴趣的主题，而非产品或具体物件
patterns.domain: 评论、个人网站相关讨论

patterns.name: 非主模式：医学论文中的 studies
patterns.context: 正式学术句中 studies 指后续研究；激活标记集中在 studies 及邻近词，并未出现前述 something 结构

en.concept: Uncertain events and their temporal boundaries
en.description: Activations often occur around generic things or events (things, something) and temporal-boundary constructions such as before/until. They span potential events, failures and repairs, disease progression, research conclusions, and project planning; other specific topics include drones, isotopes, and hardware comparisons.

patterns.name: Broadly unspecified objects/events
patterns.context: Refers to an unspecified phenomenon, failure, outcome, or event, especially near constructions such as “seeing,” “until,” and “must … before”
patterns.domain: Forum discussions, science interviews, academic abstracts, and business emails

patterns.name: Temporal boundaries and event occurrence
patterns.context: Describes a state or event that must occur before another event, or continue until something happens; often linked to outcomes such as “something,” “fails,” or “damage”
patterns.domain: Technology discussions, medical papers, news, and email

patterns.name: Unknown quantity or object
patterns.context: Occurs when an object or quantity is unspecified and referred to generically; trigger positions vary across passages
patterns.domain: Engineering, aviation, medicine, and general discussion

patterns.name: Conditional questions about repair and failure
patterns.context: Asks or describes questions about damage, repair, failure, and their thresholds

patterns.name: Future expectations or judgments
patterns.context: Discusses possible future events or disease progression, often using conditional, probabilistic, or predictive language

patterns.name: Drone regulation and potential accidents
patterns.context: Mentions drones, FAA regulation, and taking control measures before potential problems occur

patterns.name: Cancer and early diagnosis
patterns.context: Notes the need to identify high-risk individuals before the disease causes significant brain damage

patterns.name: Medical conclusions not yet established
patterns.context: States that research progress or insufficient evidence does not yet permit a definite conclusion

patterns.name: Nuclear medicine isotope supply
patterns.context: News accounts mention people who need isotopes for medical testing

patterns.name: Estimating staffing needs after a project ends
patterns.context: Assumes a project stops and estimates staffing needs before replacement work becomes available

patterns.name: Price points and processor performance comparison
patterns.context: Compares CPU prices and multithreaded performance; the following sentence is truncated

9_2194.concept: 未定事态及其时间界限
9_2194.description: 激活多出现在泛指事物或事件（things、something）以及 before/until 等时间界限结构中，涵盖潜在事件、故障与维修、疾病进展、研究结论和项目规划；另有无人机、同位素及硬件比较等具体话题。

patterns.name: 广义不确定对象/事态
patterns.context: 指代未具体说明的现象、故障、结果或事件，尤其出现在“seeing”“until”“must … before”等结构附近
patterns.domain: 论坛讨论、科普访谈、学术摘要及商务邮件

patterns.name: 时间界限与事态发生
patterns.context: 描述某状态或事件必须在另一事件之前发生，或持续到某事发生；常与“something”“fails”“damage”等结果相连
patterns.domain: 科技讨论、医学论文、新闻及邮件

patterns.name: 未知数量与对象
patterns.context: 在对象或数量未明确、仅作泛指时出现；各段触发位置不一
patterns.domain: 工程、航空、医学及一般讨论

patterns.name: 修理与失效的条件问句
patterns.trigger: “How broken must something be before it can be repaired?”；“until something fails”
patterns.context: 围绕物品损坏、维修、失效及其阈值进行提问或叙述

patterns.name: 面向未来的预期或判断
patterns.trigger: “would be seeing things” “good chance of seeing something … happening” “will develop … before”
patterns.context: 讨论可能发生的未来事件或疾病进展，常有条件、概率或预测表达
patterns.domain: 论坛讨论、访谈、医学论文

patterns.name: 无人机监管与潜在事故
patterns.context: 谈及无人机、FAA监管及在潜在问题发生前采取控制措施

patterns.name: 癌症及早期诊断
patterns.context: 指出在疾病造成显著脑损伤前识别高风险个体的需求

patterns.name: 医学结论尚待确立
patterns.context: 说明研究进展或证据不足，尚不能得出确定结论

patterns.name: 核医学同位素供给
patterns.context: 新闻叙述中提到需要同位素进行医学检测的人群

patterns.name: 项目停止后的人员需求推算
patterns.context: 假设停止项目，估算人员在替代工作出现前的需求

patterns.name: 价格点与处理器性能比较
patterns.context: 比较CPU价格与多线程性能，后句被截断

en.description: Activations cluster around generic something and its follow-up descriptions, and also occur in would hypotheticals and should choice questions; the shared theme is expression about an unspecified thing or situation.

patterns.name: would in questions
patterns.context: Embedded in dialogue or a hypothetical scenario to ask what someone would do or how something would develop; passages 1 and 2 also use it for prediction or counterfactuals.

patterns.name: something referring to a generic thing
patterns.context: Refers to an unspecified thing, followed by details about its properties, use, or flaws; especially in “something very similar,” “something it doesn’t have,” “something that ...,” “something else,” and “about something ...”.
patterns.domain: Software and product discussions, reviews, personal writing

patterns.name: Questions about choosing a thing/product
patterns.context: Asks which new car to buy as part of a set of test questions.
patterns.domain: Test or Q&A text in email

9_2194.description: 激活集中在泛指事物的 something 及其后续描述，也出现在 would 假设句和 should 选择问句中；共同点是围绕未定事物或情形展开表达。

patterns.name: 疑问句中的 would
patterns.context: 嵌在对话或假设情境中，用来询问某人会怎么做或某事会如何发展；第 1、2 段也出现预测或反事实用法。
patterns.domain: 叙事、软件讨论、一般问答

patterns.name: 泛指事物的 something
patterns.trigger: «something»，常见于“something ...”及其后接描述或关系从句
patterns.context: 指尚未具体说明的事物，后续补充性质、用途或缺陷；尤其见于“something very similar”“something it doesn’t have”“something that ...”“something else”“about something ...”。
patterns.domain: 软件与产品讨论、评论、个人写作

patterns.name: 事物／产品选择问句
patterns.context: 在一组测试问题中询问应买哪种新车。
patterns.domain: 邮件中的测试或问答文本

en.concept: English function words and modal expressions
en.description: Activations are scattered across various English function words and expressions: must, would, something, else, until, how, and a word fragment from Montenegro. Only must and would occur in two passages each, with no unified semantic or syntactic pattern overall.

patterns.name: Modal complement after must
patterns.context: Activation falls on must in predicate constructions after the subject, expressing necessary action or necessary inference; it may be followed by be, have, or another verb.

patterns.name: Questions or hypotheticals with would
patterns.context: would occurs in a question or hypothetical conditional predicate, followed by happen; passage 4 reads “What would you have done?”.

patterns.name: Description following something
patterns.context: something is an indefinite pronoun followed by similar, describing an outstanding item in an agreement.

patterns.name: Exclusion expressed with else
patterns.context: nothing else occurs in a philosophical argument, emphasizing that there is nothing else to discuss or refer to.

patterns.name: Proper-name fragment in Montenegro
patterns.context: Activation falls within the country name Montenegro, split across subwords; no clear syntactic trigger.

patterns.name: Temporal boundary with until
patterns.context: Indicates that two examination methods must be used together until whole-body MRI equipment becomes widespread; activation is strongest, but no clear pattern recurs in other passages.

patterns.name: Question introduced by how
patterns.context: “how is this happening?” introduces a question about a biological mechanism.

9_2194.concept: 英语功能词及情态表达
9_2194.description: 激活分散在多种英语功能词和表达上：must、would、something、else、until、how，以及Montenegro的分词片段；仅must和would各在两段出现，整体缺少统一语义或句法模式。

patterns.name: must 后的情态补语
patterns.trigger: « must»（第 7、10 段）；« must»« have»（第 6 段）
patterns.context: 激活落在 must，出现在主语之后、表示必要行为或必然推断的谓语结构中；前后可接 be、have 或其他动词。
patterns.domain: 邮件、技术问答、法律文本

patterns.name: would 后的疑问或假设
patterns.context: would 位于疑问句或假设性条件的谓语中，后接 happen；第 4 段为“What would you have done?”。

patterns.name: something 后的描述
patterns.context: something 用作不定代词，后接 similar，描述待办协议事项。

patterns.name: else 的排除表达
patterns.context: nothing else 出现在哲学论证中，强调除此之外别无可谈或可指涉之物。

patterns.name: Montenegro 专名片段
patterns.context: 激活落在被分词拆开的国名 Montenegro 内部；没有明显的句法触发条件。
patterns.domain: 人物列表、维基百科条目

patterns.name: until 的时间界限
patterns.context: 表示两种检查方法需要并用，直到全身 MRI 设备普及；激活强度最高，但没有与其他段重复的明显模式。

patterns.name: how 引导提问
patterns.context: how is this happening? 引出对生物机制的追问。

en.description: Primarily responds to word sequences carrying the core of questions and hypothetical questions, especially something/else/what/how, interrogative structures, and following clauses; topics span technology, mathematics, business, personal narratives, and lifestyle commentary rather than a single domain concept.

patterns.name: Asking whether other possibilities exist
patterns.context: States known facts, a solution, or an example, then asks what other options, explanations, or things exist; “else” and nearby interrogative structures are salient triggers.

patterns.name: Asking whether something is wrong or missing
patterns.context: The speaker is unsure about their understanding, code, or previous statement and asks whether something is wrong, omitted, or misunderstood.
patterns.domain: Q&A sites, especially programming and technical Q&A

patterns.name: Counterfactual challenge: “Why change it?”
patterns.context: First says the existing approach is not problematic, then questions the need for a fix or change; activation covers “something” and the following clause.

patterns.name: Asking what action can be taken
patterns.context: Raises a loss, problem, or concern, then asks whether there is a remedy.
patterns.domain: Popular science or discussions of health and social issues

patterns.name: Asking what one would do in a hypothetical situation
patterns.context: Describes a situation that has occurred, then invites readers to imagine what action they would take.
patterns.domain: Personal narratives, moral or social scenarios

patterns.name: Asking how an object would appear in a proof
patterns.context: Poses a hypothetical question about a mathematical object or proof method, asking what form or behavior the object would have under specific conditions.

patterns.name: Complaint about missing content or features
patterns.context: In reviewing a game or product, acknowledges that criticizing it for lacking something may be unfair, but still expresses disappointment about the missing feature.

patterns.name: Asking why a product needs added value
patterns.context: Discusses the business model of a product, tool, or service, arguing that simple, reliable, ready-to-use things are hard to sell or monetize.

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问与假设性提问中承载问题核心的词串，尤其 something/else/what/how、疑问结构及后接从句；话题跨技术、数学、商业、个人叙事与生活评论，并非单一领域概念。

patterns.name: 询问是否存在其他可能
patterns.context: 先陈述已知事实、方案或例子，随后询问还有什么其他选项、解释或事物；“else”及其附近的疑问结构是显著触发项。

patterns.name: 询问是否有问题或遗漏
patterns.context: 说话者对自己的理解、代码或前述说法感到不确定，询问是否有某处错误、遗漏或自己没理解之处。
patterns.domain: 问答网站，尤其编程与技术问答

patterns.name: 反事实式“为什么要改”质疑
patterns.context: 先表达原有做法没有问题，再质疑修复或改动的必要性；激活覆盖“something”及后续从句。

patterns.name: 询问可以采取什么行动
patterns.trigger: “Is there anything that can be done about it?”
patterns.context: 先提出某种损失、问题或困扰，再询问是否有补救办法。
patterns.domain: 科普或健康、社会问题讨论

patterns.name: 询问假设情形下会怎么做
patterns.context: 叙述某个已发生的情境后，邀请读者设想自己会采取何种行动。
patterns.domain: 个人叙事、道德或社交情境讨论

patterns.name: 询问证明时对象会如何呈现
patterns.context: 围绕数学对象或证明方法提出假设性问题，询问对象在特定条件下的形式或表现。

patterns.name: 缺失内容或功能的抱怨
patterns.context: 评价游戏或产品时，承认批评其不具备某项内容可能不公平，但仍表达对缺失功能的失望。

patterns.name: 询问商品为何需要附加价值
patterns.context: 讨论产品、工具或服务的商业模式，认为简单可靠、开箱即用的东西不易销售或变现。

en.description: Activations cluster around indefinite objects such as something/anything in existential constructions with there is/is there, especially in questions expressing uncertainty or requesting help; they also occur in copyright disclaimers and related contexts asking about errors, causes, or responses.

patterns.name: Uncertain object in an existential construction
patterns.context: Uses an existential sentence to ask about something not yet identified, understood, or addressed; often accompanied by a question or conditional clause.
patterns.domain: Q&A, forum discussions, and explanatory text

patterns.name: Help-seeking questions expressing uncertainty
patterns.context: The speaker faces confusion about code, mathematics, or a phenomenon and asks whether information is missing, what is wrong, or what the cause is.
patterns.domain: StackExchange, HackerNews, and general online discussions

patterns.name: Problem statement in a legal disclaimer
patterns.context: A conditional sentence states that a copy may have a problem, appearing in copyright or liability text; the same disclaimer recurs.

patterns.name: Response to injustice or error
patterns.context: First states that an action or assumption is unfair or wrong, then asks readers how to respond.

patterns.name: Causal question introduced by “could”
patterns.context: Asks how a condition could cause an outcome in a web interaction; no “something is” construction appears.

9_2194.description: 激活集中在 something/anything 等不定对象与 there is/is there 构成的存在表达，尤其是疑惑、求助式提问；另见版权免责声明，以及追问错误、原因或应对方式的相近语境。

patterns.name: 存在结构中的不确定对象
patterns.trigger: “there is something”“there’s something”“is there anything”，以及“something … here”“anything that can be done”
patterns.context: 围绕存在句提出尚未识别、理解或处理的事物；常伴随疑问或条件语句。
patterns.domain: 问答、论坛讨论及说明性文字

patterns.name: 求助式的疑惑提问
patterns.trigger: “Is there something …?”、“Is there something I’m missing?”、“what else …?”、“How could …?”
patterns.context: 说话者面对代码、数学或现象中的困惑，询问是否遗漏信息、哪里出错或原因是什么。

patterns.name: 法律免责声明中的问题陈述
patterns.trigger: “if there is something wrong with your copy”
patterns.context: 以条件句说明副本可能有问题，处于版权声明或免责文字中；同一声明重复出现。
patterns.domain: Gutenberg 电子书前置法律说明

patterns.name: 对不公或错误的反应
patterns.context: 先陈述某种做法或假设不公、错误，再向读者征询如何反应。
patterns.domain: 个人叙事、评论性网络文字

patterns.name: “could”引出的因果疑问
patterns.trigger: “How could a rollover state cause this”
patterns.context: 针对网页交互现象追问某个状态如何造成结果；未出现“something is”句式。

en.concept: The English existential construction “there is something”
en.description: Activations cluster around the English construction “there is something”: in dialogue, it raises an existential question or conjecture, followed by various complements such as anything, wrong, here, I’m missing, and to complain; topics and styles span business, programming, mathematics, social interaction, and legal text.

patterns.name: The there is something construction
patterns.context: Used to ask or conjecture whether there is an object, cause, problem, omission, or something to rely on; often followed by a modifier, with no required specific continuation.
patterns.domain: Forum Q&A, online discussions, explanatory text, and literary text

9_2194.description: 激活集中在英语构式 “there is something”：对话中以其提出存在性疑问或猜测，后接 anything、wrong、here、I’m missing、to complain 等不同补语；话题和文体跨商业、编程、数学、社交及法律文本。

patterns.name: there is something 构式
patterns.context: 在询问或推测某处是否有某物、某个原因、问题、遗漏或可依靠的东西时，常接后续限定语；不要求特定后续词。
patterns.domain: 论坛问答、网络讨论、说明文字及文学文本

en.description: Primarily responds to “Is there(something/anything)…” in questions, especially when requesting troubleshooting, checking for omissions, or asking about differences; it also occurs in code help, seeking remedies, evidence, or additional content.

patterns.name: Existential question structure
patterns.context: Asks whether there is an omission, problem, or noteworthy thing; often paired with following content such as something, wrong, missing, or different.
patterns.domain: Q&A, forum discussions, and general explanatory prose

patterns.name: Questioning a state of affairs or one’s understanding
patterns.context: Describes code, a rule, or an opinion, then asks whether it is wrong or whether the speaker has misunderstood; some instances connect to existential questions.

patterns.name: Technical help request after a code snippet
patterns.context: After presenting code or a query problem, asks whether the implementation, form, or query contains an error; the passage often sits near code, error messages, or technical terms.

patterns.name: Asking about analogous tools or features
patterns.context: Asks whether an alternative exists for a product or service that is similar to a known tool.

patterns.name: Asking whether there is a remedy
patterns.context: States a problem and its effects, then asks whether any action can resolve it.

patterns.name: Asking about differences or additional content
patterns.context: Asks whether a category of product has any differences or whether there is extra, worthwhile content to view.

patterns.name: Seeking a reason to rely on
patterns.context: In an argument or statement of position, seeks grounds that can still be relied upon or maintained.

patterns.name: Combining uncertainty with a request for explanation
patterns.context: Describes anomalous behavior or an unknown cause, then asks whether some factor is causing the problem; overlaps with technical help-seeking.

9_2194.description: 主要响应疑问句中的“Is there(something/anything)…”，尤其在请求排查、确认是否遗漏或追问差异时；也出现在代码求助、寻求补救、依据或额外内容等语境。

patterns.name: 存在疑问句式
patterns.context: 在询问是否存在遗漏、问题或值得注意的事物；常与 something、wrong、missing、different 等后续内容搭配。
patterns.domain: 问答、论坛讨论及一般说明文

patterns.name: 对现状或理解提出疑问
patterns.trigger: “Is … wrong?”、“Is the Coding Guide wrong?”、“I don’t get”
patterns.context: 先描述代码、规则或观点，再询问其是否错误或自己是否理解有误；部分与存在疑问句式相连。

patterns.name: 代码片段后的技术求助
patterns.context: 展示代码或查询问题后，询问实现、表单或查询是否有错误；段中常紧邻代码、错误信息或技术名词。

patterns.name: 工具或功能类比询问
patterns.context: 询问某产品或服务是否存在类似于已知工具的替代品。

patterns.name: 询问是否有补救办法
patterns.trigger: “is there anything that can be done about it?”
patterns.context: 先陈述问题及其影响，再询问是否能采取措施解决。
patterns.domain: 新闻或生活类说明文字

patterns.name: 询问差异或额外内容
patterns.trigger: “Is there something different about”及“there is something extra”
patterns.context: 询问某类产品是否有不同之处，或某处是否存在额外、值得查看的内容。

patterns.name: 寻找可依凭的理由
patterns.trigger: “Surely there is something to cling on to here”
patterns.context: 在争论或立场表达中，寻求仍可依赖或坚持的依据。

patterns.name: 不确定性与求解释的组合
patterns.trigger: “I don’t know what’s happening”后接“Is there something … messing this up”
patterns.context: 描述行为异常或原因不明，再询问是否有某个因素导致问题；与技术求助模式重叠。

en.description: Primarily responds to interrogative expressions that locate a problem, error, or anomaly, especially “something/wrong,” “What’s wrong,” and “What could be the problem”; it also responds to questions about omissions and remedies, as well as statements identifying an issue to fix.

patterns.name: Locating a problem in a help-seeking question
patterns.context: After describing a failure, error, or anomaly, the questioner asks what is wrong, what caused it, or requests troubleshooting help; common in StackExchange technical Q&A.
patterns.domain: Technical support, programming, and system-failure Q&A

patterns.name: Asking whether something is missing or a solution is available
patterns.context: Uses a question to explore omissions, remedies, or additional information; does not necessarily describe a specific technical error.
patterns.domain: Technical Q&A, health or social issues, everyday discussions

patterns.name: Identifying something that needs fixing
patterns.context: First reports an issue with a website or service, then identifies a problem that needs to be addressed; not a help-seeking question.
patterns.domain: HackerNews website operations or outage notices

9_2194.description: 主要响应对问题、错误或异常的疑问式定位表达，尤其是“something/wrong”“What’s wrong”“What could be the problem”；也响应询问遗漏、解决办法，以及指出待修复事项。

patterns.name: 疑问式求助中的问题定位
patterns.trigger: “What is wrong”, “What’s wrong”, “something wrong”, “What could be the problem”, “must be something wrong”
patterns.context: 提问者描述故障、错误或异常后，询问哪里出错、原因是什么，或请求帮助排查；常见于 StackExchange 技术问答。
patterns.domain: 技术支持、编程与系统故障问答

patterns.name: 询问是否遗漏或有可行办法
patterns.trigger: “Is there something I’m missing?”, “Is there anything that can be done about it?”, “there is something extra”
patterns.context: 以疑问形式探寻遗漏、解决办法或额外信息；不一定描述明确的技术错误。
patterns.domain: 技术问答、健康或社会议题、日常讨论

patterns.name: 发现需要修复之处
patterns.context: 先报告网站或服务异常，再指出需要处理的问题；不是求助式提问。
patterns.domain: HackerNews 网站运营或故障公告

en.description: Activations often occur around unknown things, causes, and possible outcomes in questions or conjectures (anything, something, what, might, would); there are also special cases such as unless in patent boilerplate and questions about paper contributions, with no single lexical pattern covering all triggers.

patterns.name: Existence or possibility in questions
patterns.context: Activation often falls on a question word or a word in a question that introduces an unknown thing, cause, or possible outcome, sometimes introduced by what/there; not all questions fit.
patterns.domain: News, forum discussions, technical Q&A, and narrative

patterns.name: unless in a patent disclaimer
patterns.context: In fixed legal/patent wording, unless introduces an exception, followed by a statement about what should not be assumed; strong activation falls on unless.

patterns.name: Introductory question in a paper abstract
patterns.context: A medical paper abstract uses a question to introduce the paper’s contribution; strong activation centers on What does this paper.

patterns.name: would in a conditional-consequence sentence
patterns.context: In legal or news discussion, would introduces a possible consequence if a court takes the previously mentioned action; strong activation falls on would.

patterns.name: something introducing an object of complaint
patterns.context: A forum comment uses there’s something to introduce something to complain about; strong activation falls on something.

9_2194.description: 激活多见于疑问或推测语境中的未知事物、原因与可能结果（anything、something、what、might、would）；另有 unless 专利套语及论文贡献问句等特例，未见能覆盖全部触发形式的单一词法模式。

patterns.name: 疑问中的存在或可能性
patterns.trigger: “anything ... can be done”“there is something extra”“what on earth had happened”“What’s wrong”“what might occur”“what else is out there”
patterns.context: 激活常落在疑问词或疑问句中承接未知事物、原因、可能结果的词上，部分由 what/there 引出；并非所有疑问句都符合。
patterns.domain: 新闻、论坛讨论、技术问答与叙述

patterns.name: 专利免责声明中的 unless
patterns.context: 固定法律/专利表述中，unless 引出例外条件，随后说明不应作何假设；强激活落在 unless。

patterns.name: 论文摘要的引导性问句
patterns.context: 医学论文摘要中，以问句引出本文贡献；强激活集中在 What does this paper。

patterns.name: 条件结果句中的 would
patterns.trigger: “that would give EPIC what it originally sought”
patterns.context: 法律/新闻论述中，假设法院采取前述措施，would 引出可能后果；强激活落在 would。

patterns.name: 抱怨引出对象的 something
patterns.context: 论坛评论中以 there’s something 引出可抱怨之事；强激活落在 something。

en.concept: Questions and introduction of unknown information
en.description: Activations are concentrated mainly in question-initial structures, especially a question word followed by a modal or auxiliary; a few declarative sentences also activate near expressions such as “what's happening” and “something extra/special.”

patterns.name: Question-initial word
patterns.context: At the start of a question or interrogative phrase; the question word is often followed by an auxiliary or copula
patterns.domain: StackExchange, HackerNews, PubMed Q&A, and general narrative

patterns.name: Modal/auxiliary in a question
patterns.context: Forms a question about a cause, possibility, or necessity after a question word
patterns.domain: Technical Q&A, academic abstract Q&A, discussion posts

patterns.name: Complement or following word in a question
patterns.context: Specifies the question, cause, or object in an interrogative sentence; trigger position varies

patterns.name: Event description following what's
patterns.context: Embedded in a declarative sentence to describe something happening; not a sentence-initial question

patterns.name: something introducing existence or specialness
patterns.context: Uses something to introduce additional information or a special property; surrounding contexts vary

patterns.name: Duplicate email sample
patterns.context: An email excerpt identical to passage 5, with the same trigger form and context

9_2194.description: 激活主要集中于疑问句起始结构，尤其疑问词后接情态或助动词；少数陈述句也在“what's happening”及“something extra/special”一类表达附近激活。

patterns.name: 疑问句起始词
patterns.context: 提问句开头或疑问短语起始处；疑问词后常接助动词或系动词

patterns.name: 疑问句中的情态/助动词
patterns.context: 疑问词之后构成询问原因、可能性或必要性的句式
patterns.domain: 技术问答、学术摘要问答、讨论帖

patterns.name: 疑问句中的补语或后续词
patterns.context: 疑问句中说明所问问题、原因或对象；触发位置不固定

patterns.name: what's 后接事件描述
patterns.context: 嵌在陈述句中，说明某事正在发生；不是句首疑问句

patterns.name: something 作存在性或特殊性引介
patterns.context: 以 something 引入额外信息或特殊性质，前后语境不同

patterns.name: 重复邮件样本
patterns.context: 与第5段内容相同的邮件片段，触发形式和上下文一致

en.description: Activation patterns are scattered: sentence-initial Because, name or proper-name fragments, formatting whitespace, and model in code paths occur separately. There is also an unclassified military readiness context from Perspectives, with no reliable common trigger feature.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial Because
patterns.context: The sentence begins with Because, followed by an explanatory clause; activation does not depend on a specific topic.

patterns.name: Names or abbreviation fragments beginning with A
patterns.context: Uppercase A appears as the initial of a name in a signature or as part of an email name string; the two examples have different contexts.

patterns.name: Utah character fragment in a proper name
patterns.context: Occurs in the place name Utah, immediately after «U»5; also appears with a report title and line break.

patterns.name: Typesetting whitespace in legal documents
patterns.context: A large span of spaces after an opinion title and before a court name; activation may be related to formatting or whitespace.

patterns.name: In-word fragment in the place name Bolivia

patterns.name: model in a JavaScript import path

patterns.name: Document-format fragment with mixed symbols and proper names
patterns.context: [4] has typesetting whitespace in a court document; [5] has the uppercase string TIWANA in a location byline. The trigger forms differ, making a common condition difficult to confirm.

en.description: Activation spans multiple genres, involving word-initial uppercase fragments, title line breaks and metadata, mathematical proof templates, sentence-initial Because, and a few military, medical, and patent terms. These local patterns cannot be explained by a single semantic topic.

patterns.name: Standalone uppercase letters or initial fragments at the start of English words
patterns.context: Activation falls on uppercase letters or fragments at word beginnings; some are followed immediately by lowercase word fragments, while others form place names, titles, or sentence-initial words.
patterns.domain: Mixed: reports, place names, medical terms, question prompts, etc.

patterns.name: Formatting structures in titles or document metadata
patterns.context: In structured text such as line-initial or multiline titles, version dates, and location and date fields, activation involves line breaks and adjacent title or field fragments.
patterns.domain: Web or document titles, location and date fields

patterns.name: Mathematical proof prompt
patterns.context: A StackExchange question begins with Q:, followed by a blank line and “Prove that” and a mathematical proposition; the propositions differ across examples.

patterns.name: Formula start in a mathematical proof
patterns.context: Same as the proof-question template, but the formula follows “Prove” directly; the fragment does not show that.

patterns.name: Sentence-initial Because
patterns.context: A sentence or text fragment begins with Because; what follows is either explanatory discussion or a causal clause.
patterns.domain: Popular-science/academic text, patent background, medical research abstracts

patterns.name: Military readiness and resilience phrase in a title
patterns.context: A report title describes military readiness and resilience; activation highlights military and the following phrase.
patterns.domain: PubMed abstract titles, military health or public health

patterns.name: Subword fragments within medical terms
patterns.context: Activation is distributed across multiple subword fragments of complex medical terms rather than one clearly complete word; the context mentions surgery.

patterns.name: Word fragment in a disease name
patterns.context: The disease name Crohn's Disease appears after sentence-initial Because.

patterns.name: Patent background phrase containing malicious worms
patterns.context: Malicious worms are mentioned in a causal background sentence beginning “Because of the increasing number of ...”; the positively activated token itself is not marked in the source text.

9_2290.description: 激活跨多种文体，涉及词首大写片段、标题换行和元数据、数学证明模板、Because句首，以及少数军事、医学和专利词汇；这些局部模式不能由单一语义主题解释。

patterns.name: 疾病名称中的分词片段

en.description: Activation often falls on internal segments of proper names, rare terms, abbreviations, compounds, and URLs. Code identifiers and boundaries also appear; the examples span domains but show no stable semantic theme.

patterns.name: Syllables within proper names
patterns.context: Strong activation falls on tokenized fragments inside proper names, URLs, or technical terms rather than consistently on complete words; some words have unusual spelling or capitalization boundaries.
patterns.domain: Mixed: email names, web URLs, scientific terminology

patterns.name: Compound words or word-initial fragments
patterns.context: Activation is concentrated on compounds, abbreviations, or in-word fragments, especially at word beginnings or internal segmentation points; this occurs in both medical text and names.

patterns.name: Identifiers and code boundaries
patterns.context: Activation occurs near class names, property names, and syntax punctuation in code, possibly favoring camelCase identifiers or list-initialization boundaries.

patterns.name: Address and date fields
patterns.context: Uppercase fields in place-name or address formats, followed by state abbreviations and dates; there is insufficient context to confirm a pattern.

patterns.name: Rare fragments in long medical terms
patterns.context: Activation occurs at internal subword boundaries in longer technical terms in biomedical passages; the surrounding text describes research or measurement equipment.

patterns.name: Titles and link text
patterns.context: A web title or news summary appears adjacent to a URL, with activation on a local fragment of the link domain; the title topics differ.

patterns.name: Inside technical compound nouns
patterns.context: In a patent technical description, activation falls on material/component names in parentheses or adjacent compound nouns.

patterns.name: Formatting/whitespace boundaries
patterns.context: Line breaks, spaces, or punctuation boundaries also show activation, but occur in a single code segment or web passage, so no independent pattern can be confirmed.

9_2290.description: 激活多落在专名、罕见术语、缩写、复合词及网址的内部切分片段，也见代码标识符和边界；跨领域但未呈现稳定语义主题。

en.description: Activation is scattered across in-word token fragments, become and its following structure, the possessive world's, and paper-title boundaries. There is also a monogamous example and a personal age-and-experience context, with no single stable semantic pattern.

patterns.name: Word-initial fragments split within words
patterns.context: Activation falls on internal fragments of segmented words; target words and positions vary, and may be surrounded by common words or proper names.
patterns.domain: General text, including forums, medical text, and institutional descriptions

patterns.name: Words after become
patterns.context: In descriptions of institutional or personal development, identity, or scale, become is marked; in some examples the immediately following article is also marked.
patterns.domain: Institutional descriptions, grant applications, and career advice

patterns.name: Possessive structure with world's
patterns.context: world is followed by 's and then by a superlative describing a person or thing.

patterns.name: Cue words near paragraph or section boundaries
patterns.context: Near the title, section markers, or opening of a medical paper; activation is distributed across words in the title and the following structure.

patterns.name: Phrase monogamous relationships
patterns.context: In a discussion of contraceptive products and relationship types, monogamous is segmented and its initial fragment is strongly activated.

patterns.name: Age and time expressions in an author's experience
patterns.context: A forum reply mentions when they began working professionally and compares their age with the other person.

9_2290.description: 激活分散在词内分词片段、become 及其后续结构、world's 所有格和论文标题边界等位置；另有 monogamous 与个人年龄经历语境，未见单一稳定语义模式。

patterns.name: 词内切分的词首片段
patterns.context: 激活落在被分词切开的词的内部片段上；目标词及其位置并不一致，周围还可能有常见词或专名
patterns.domain: 通用文本，包含论坛、医学及机构介绍

patterns.name: become 后的词
patterns.trigger: «grown»7« to»6« become»10« the»5« Group»2；«grown»6« to»5« become»9« the»4« largest»6；«become»9« academ»2icians
patterns.context: 在描述机构或个人发展、身份或规模变化时，become 被标记；部分例子中紧邻其后的冠词也标记
patterns.domain: 机构介绍、资助申请及职业建议

patterns.name: world's 的所有格结构
patterns.context: world 后接 's，并继续以最高级描述人物或事物

patterns.name: 段落或章节边界附近的引导词
patterns.context: 医学论文的标题、章节标记或引言开头附近；激活分布在标题词内部及其后续结构

patterns.name: 作者经历中的年龄与时间表达
patterns.context: 论坛回复中谈及开始职业工作的时间及与对方年龄的比较

en.description: The most prominent recurring clue is become/becoming followed by an identity or state, but other strong activations are scattered across insurance, individual in-word fragments, and medical and career contexts; no single pattern explains all passages.

patterns.name: Identity, state, or degree following become
patterns.context: Activation is concentrated on the article and identity, occupation, state, or degree word following become/becoming; not every instance of become is equally strong.
patterns.domain: General narration, career and personal experience

patterns.name: In-word fragment of monogamous
patterns.context: Occurs in a sentence about condoms and relationships; activation mainly falls within the segmented word.

patterns.name: Health insurance terminology
patterns.context: Clear activation occurs near a health-insurance entry subheading and terminology explanation; “In” reaches the highest intensity in this batch.

patterns.name: Nursing-home care and country comparison
patterns.context: A study of end-of-life care in nursing homes transitions to a comparison of doctors' work arrangements in Norway and the Netherlands; the strongest activation falls on Norway.

patterns.name: Job search and work experience of an entrepreneur
patterns.context: An HN help-seeking post describes a solo entrepreneur looking for consulting work; activation falls on been, working, and nearby words.
patterns.domain: Hacker News, entrepreneurship and career advice

patterns.name: Innovation/disruption phrasing in a Doctor of Nursing Practice
patterns.context: The title and abstract opening of a nursing education paper; activation is distributed across subword fragments of professional and institutional names.

9_2290.description: 最突出的重复线索是 become/becoming 后接身份或状态，但其余强激活分散于保险、单个词内片段、医学与职业语境；没有一个模式能解释全部段落。

patterns.name: become 后接身份、状态或程度
patterns.trigger: “become”及其后的补语，如 “become an independent investigator”“becoming an unbalanced workaholic”“become a little obsessed”
patterns.context: 激活集中在 become/becoming 后面的冠词及身份、职业、状态或程度词；并非每个 become 都同样强。
patterns.domain: 一般叙述、职业与个人经历

patterns.name: monogamous 的词内片段
patterns.context: 出现在关于避孕套及关系的句子中，激活主要落在被拆分的词内部。

patterns.name: 健康保险术语
patterns.context: 健康保险条目小标题和术语说明附近有明显激活；“In”达到本批最高强度。

patterns.name: 养老护理与国家对比
patterns.context: 养老院临终护理研究中转入挪威与荷兰医生工作安排的比较；最强激活落在 Norway。

patterns.name: 创业者求职与工作经历
patterns.context: HN 求助帖描述单人创业者寻找咨询工作；激活落在 been、working 及其附近。

patterns.name: 护理实践博士的创新／颠覆表述
patterns.context: 护理教育论文标题及摘要开头；激活分布在专业名称和机构名称的词片段上。

en.description: The strongest common clue is a transition in career identity or status (becoming, started working, turned professional), especially an independent research career. Other activation is scattered across medical research, occupational categories, language names, and Portuguese historical terms, without a unified meaning.

patterns.name: becoming/career identity
patterns.context: Strong responses cluster around “becoming an …” and the following noun phrase denoting an identity, occupational role, or status; contexts concern career development, career choices, or research careers.
patterns.domain: Personal career narratives, research career development

patterns.name: Narrative of age and starting work
patterns.context: First-person conversation introduces the experience of starting work through an age comparison; activation falls near “was”.

patterns.name: Doctor–patient relationship research wording
patterns.context: An academic abstract discusses doctor–patient relationships, communication, or research design; notable activation occurs around “in many”.

patterns.name: Institutional personnel category terms
patterns.context: A list or regulatory context enumerates business categories such as manufacturers, assemblers, importers, and distributors; activation is concentrated on the in-word fragment “Im”.

patterns.name: Representation in medical professions
patterns.context: Discusses the underrepresentation of population groups in medicine, dentistry, allied health fields, and academia; strong activation falls on “dental”.

patterns.name: Portuguese place/language name
patterns.context: A page listing languages and their local written names in HTML language preferences; activation falls on “Rom”.

patterns.name: Portuguese word form for “historical interweaving”
patterns.context: Portuguese philosophical discussion describes an unintended result formed by the interweaving of many historical actions; activation falls on “hist”.

patterns.name: Becoming a professional player in a biography
patterns.context: A biography narrates an athlete's birth information and early career before becoming a professional; activation is concentrated on “turned”.

9_2290.description: 最强共同线索是职业身份或状态的转变（becoming、started working、turned professional），尤其科研独立职业；其余激活分散于医学研究、职业类别、语言名和葡语历史词等局部片段，缺乏统一语义。

patterns.name: becoming／career身份
patterns.trigger: becoming an unbalanced workaholic；becoming a successful independent researcher；to become an independent investigator
patterns.context: 强响应集中在“becoming an …”及其后表示身份、职业角色或状态的名词短语；上下文谈职业发展、职业选择或研究生涯。
patterns.domain: 个人职业叙述、科研职业发展

patterns.name: 年龄与工作起步叙述
patterns.trigger: older than you and started working professionally when I was your age
patterns.context: 第一人称对话中以年龄比较引出开始工作的经历；激活落在“was”附近。

patterns.name: doctor–patient关系研究措辞
patterns.trigger: in many studies, doctors and patients
patterns.context: 学术摘要中讨论医生与患者关系、沟通或研究设计；明显激活出现在“in many”一带。
patterns.domain: 医学／健康服务研究摘要

patterns.name: 机构人员类别词
patterns.context: 列表或法规语境中列举制造商、装配商、进口商、经销商等商业类别；激活集中在词内片段“Im”。

patterns.name: 医疗职业代表性

patterns.context: 讨论人口群体在医疗、牙科、相关健康领域及学术界的代表性不足；强激活落在“dental”。
patterns.domain: 公共卫生／人口统计论述

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语地名／语言名
patterns.context: HTML语言偏好页面中列举语言及其本地书写名称；激活落在“Rom”。

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语“历史交织”词形
patterns.context: 葡萄牙语哲学论述中，描述由众多历史行动交织形成的非预期结果；激活落在“hist”。

patterns.name: 人物传记中的转为职业球手
patterns.context: 传记以出生信息和早期生涯叙述运动员成为职业选手；激活集中在“turned”。

en.description: Activations commonly occur in personal accounts and biographies, and also cover Portuguese or language names, web-format markers, and contexts such as relationship health, biography, and mental health policy. No clear, unified semantic trigger is apparent across samples.

patterns.name: Self-introductions and personal experiences
patterns.context: First-person accounts of personal identity, upbringing, work experience, or seeking advice; common in Q&A, interviews, and personal biographies.

patterns.name: Portuguese and other-language text
patterns.context: Occurs in Portuguese body text or webpage language selectors; activations fall on subword fragments of words with diacritics and language names.

patterns.name: Layout and formatting boundaries
patterns.context: Near page line breaks, section headings, or post titles, including webpage structure or text segmentation.

patterns.name: Relationship and sexual health discussions
patterns.context: Discusses contraceptive products and their use in committed relationships.

patterns.name: Biographical accounts of historical figures
patterns.context: Describes a person's identity, aliases, and personal relationships.

patterns.name: Mental health policy terminology
patterns.context: Discusses the community mental health services market and related policy administration.

9_2290.description: 激活常见于个人自述与简介，也覆盖葡萄牙语或语言名称、网页格式标记，以及关系健康、传记和心理健康政策等语境；不同样本间未见统一的明确语义触发点。

patterns.name: 自我介绍与个人经历
patterns.trigger: “I'm a struggling single-founder”“I am asking”“I grew up”“I was”

patterns.name: 葡萄牙语及其他语言文本
patterns.context: 出现在葡萄牙语正文或网页语言选择器中；激活落在带变音符号的词及语言名称的子词上。
